# Additions to Daniel Chapter 3 (Bel and the Dragon) — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus (Theodotion recension), Additions to Daniel 3
**Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADD_003_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Decision

Bel and the Dragon is satire and wonder-tale. The tone is different from either the Susanna detective story (taut, legal) or the Benedicite (liturgical). Here the author invites the reader to laugh — Daniel laughs twice (vv. 7, 18), and the double laugh is a characterization device. The king is gullible but ultimately just. The Habakkuk episode is pure folklore with a kind of absurdist joy. PNEUMA's pacing and wit are adopted for the central comedic scenes (vv. 5–21, 23–26); LOGOS provides precision for the theological declarations (vv. 5, 24, 37, 40, 42).

---

**1** King Astyages was gathered to his fathers, and Cyrus the Persian received the kingdom.

**2** Daniel was a companion of the king and more honored than all his other friends.

**3** Now the Babylonians had an idol called Bel, and every day twelve large measures of fine flour, forty sheep, and six jars of wine were consumed for it.

**4** The king honored it and went every day to worship it; but Daniel worshiped his own God.

**5** The king said to him: "Why do you not worship Bel?" He answered: "Because I do not worship idols made by human hands, but the living God, who created heaven and earth and has dominion over all flesh."

**6** The king said: "Does it not seem obvious to you that Bel is alive? Do you not see how much he eats and drinks every single day?"

**7** Daniel laughed. "Do not be deceived, O king — this is clay on the inside and bronze on the outside. It has never eaten or drunk a single thing."

**8** The king turned furious and summoned his priests. He said to them: "Unless you tell me who is consuming these provisions, you will die.

**9** But if you can show that Bel eats them, Daniel shall die, for he has spoken blasphemy against Bel." Daniel said to the king: "Let it be as you say."

**10** Now the priests of Bel numbered seventy, besides wives and children. The king went with Daniel into the temple of Bel.

**11** The priests of Bel said: "We ourselves will leave, O king; you set out the food and mix the wine, seal the doors, and come early in the morning. If you do not find that Bel has eaten everything, we will die; otherwise Daniel shall die, who has lied against us."

**12** They were not worried, for they had made a hidden entrance under the table and always came in through it and consumed everything.

**13** After they had gone, the king set the food before Bel. Then Daniel ordered his servants to bring ashes, and they strewed them over the entire floor of the temple in the king's presence alone; then they went out, sealed the door, and departed.

**14** In the night the priests came as usual with their wives and children, and ate and drank everything.

**15** The king rose early in the morning, and Daniel with him.

**16** The king said: "Daniel, are the seals intact?" He replied: "Intact, O king."

**17** As soon as the doors were opened, the king looked at the table and cried out with a loud voice: "Great are you, O Bel! There is no deception in you at all!"

**18** But Daniel laughed, and held the king back from going in, and said: "Look at the floor and see whose footprints these are."

**19** The king said: "I see the footprints of men and women and children." And the king was enraged.

**20** He seized the priests and their wives and children; and they showed him the hidden entrance through which they used to come in and consume the provisions on the table.

**21** The king put them to death and gave Bel over to Daniel, who demolished it and its temple.

**22** Now in that place there was a great dragon, and the Babylonians worshiped it.

**23** The king said to Daniel: "You cannot say that this one is not a living god — therefore worship it."

**24** Daniel answered: "I worship the Lord my God, for he is the living God.

**25** But give me permission, O king, and I will kill the dragon — without sword or weapon." The king said: "I give you permission."

**26** Daniel took pitch and fat and hair, and cooked them together and made cakes, and put them into the dragon's mouth. The dragon ate them and burst open. And Daniel said: "Look what you were worshiping!"

**27** When the Babylonians heard what had happened, they were furious and conspired against the king, saying: "The king has turned Jew; he has overthrown Bel, killed the dragon, and slaughtered the priests."

**28** They came to the king and said: "Hand Daniel over to us, or we will kill you and your household."

**29** The king saw that they were pressing heavily against him, and under compulsion he handed Daniel over to them.

**30** They threw him into the lions' den, and he was there for six days.

**31** In the den there were seven lions, and they had been given two human bodies and two sheep each day; but now these were withheld, so that they would devour Daniel.

**32** Now in Judea there was the prophet Habakkuk, who had made a stew and crumbled bread into a bowl, and was on his way to the field to bring it to the harvesters.

**33** The angel of the Lord said to Habakkuk: "Take the meal you have to Babylon, to Daniel who is in the lions' den."

**34** Habakkuk said: "Lord, I have never seen Babylon and I do not know where the den is."

**35** The angel of the Lord took him by the crown of his head and carried him by his hair, and with a blast of his breath set him down in Babylon, directly above the den.

**36** Habakkuk called out: "Daniel! Daniel! Take the meal that God has sent you."

**37** Daniel said: "You have remembered me, O God; you have not forsaken those who love you."

**38** Daniel got up and ate. And the angel of God immediately returned Habakkuk to his own place.

**39** On the seventh day the king came to mourn for Daniel. He came to the den and looked in — and there was Daniel, sitting there.

**40** The king cried out with a loud voice: "Great are you, O Lord God of Daniel! There is no god but you!"

**41** He drew Daniel out, and those who had sought his destruction he cast into the den; and they were devoured in an instant before his eyes.

**42** Then the king declared: "Let all who inhabit the earth fear the God of Daniel, for he is the Savior, who works signs and wonders in the earth, and who has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions."
